method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md. Atomscan and cleave facts on each original; Rizin and dnfile/dncil static execution-path analysis. No specimen execution or endpoint contact.
external_context: The three supplied Triage pages were inaccessible. Collector filenames and model verdicts were not treated as proof; no deployment authorization was supplied.

samples.identification: BorderCheckpoint cover application with bitmap-concealed managed loader
evidence: The ZIP contains one .NET PE named PO #4713582.scr. Its unsigned version fields claim Microsoft and BorderCheckpoint, with OriginalFilename IScS.exe. The name alone is not a conviction.
e1m constructor at RVA 0x2c68 calls H15 (RVA 0x51a8), which executes the concealed load path during form construction. Reactor control-flow flattening intersperses UI setup with payload dispatch.
OPlus bitmap at file offset 0x14cc3 is 147x147. Pj7.FjX (RVA 0xa71c) traverses GetPixel(x,y) by columns and appends R,G,B, capped at 64512 bytes. Reconstruction yields a managed PE.
H15 calls GetDomain().Load(ToArray(bytes)), selects GetTypes()[1].GetMethods()[0], and invokes its Invoke member through VB LateCall with a string-array argument. The selected method is Form1.Justy.

The delimiter-separated initializer supplies hex 6268594C (bhYL), hex 666479 (fdy), and BorderCheckpoint. Justy sleeps through a delegate to Thread.Sleep with 24005, decodes those hex strings, and retrieves the bhYL resource bitmap.

The second bitmap is a 1103x1151 PNG at 0x2ac60. RestoreOriginalBitmap subtracts 177 columns and 225 rows, leaving a 926x926 square. The decoder packs BGRA in column order, reads a 3423745-byte length prefix, and extracts that buffer.

Mist XORs each byte with the last byte XOR 112 and a repeating key. It encodes fdy in UTF-16BE but wraps the index at the character count, so the effective repeating bytes are 00 66 00. Recovery produces another valid managed assembly.

The recovered assembly is loaded with the late-bound AppDomain Load path and dispatched by GetTypes()[7].GetMethods()[17]. Concealed executable resources, automatic invocation, multiple changing application identities and the attachment disguise establish deception beyond image processing.
samples.limits: No runtime success, ultimate malware family, credential theft, C2, or ransomware claim. The final recovered assembly remains protected; no unsupported payload behavior is added.

samples.identification: StormAttack installer with erased DLL resource directory
evidence: PE entry 0x402674 reaches main 0x401cb0. Mode dword at 0x404120 is 3, reaching 0x401900 and then self-delete helper 0x401390.

0x401900 constructs an HKLM Active Setup Installed Components subkey, writes StubPath as REG_EXPAND_SZ at 0x401a4b, reads its own module using CRT I/O, patches its buffer, writes a copy and launches it.
0x401390 obtains its own module path, converts it to an 8.3 short path, reads COMSPEC and constructs /c del with > nul before CreateProcessA.

Additional code at 0x401260 opens LanmanServer Parameters, deletes ServiceDLL and replaces it with an alternate DLL path. 0x401150 creates a target process, allocates remote memory, writes the DLL path and starts a thread at resolved LoadLibraryA.
Family banners and StormServer.dll corroborate the code identity. The .rsrc section is entirely zero and its resource directory has zero entries, so extraction cannot supply a usable embedded DLL.
samples.limits: Malicious installer code is retained, but successful persistence, DLL execution, DDoS, Remcos or WannaCry behavior is not established. Code defects do not imply a benign product.

samples.identification: StormAttack installer with padded call trampoline and damaged DLL
evidence: The main .text bytes match the other StormAttack installer except for the five-byte call site at 0x401f8f. Both use mode 3 and contain the same Active Setup, registry hijack, DLL-injection and shell cleanup routines.

At 0x401f8f the modified code jumps to RWX .htext at 0x40f000, calls the original self-delete routine, traverses canceling byte INC/DEC and self-exchange/self-move padding, then jumps back at 0x40f40e to 0x401f94.
Resource DLL/101/2052 contains 39936 bytes, only 2200 nonzero. It retains Storm ddos DNS and STORM command format strings, but has a zeroed entrypoint, damaged imports and no executable section.
DLL injection uses a resolved LoadLibraryA address as the remote-thread entry. Mode-1 ServiceDLL replacement is a code capability, not an assertion it executes in mode 3.
samples.limits: No working embedded DLL, active flood, credential theft, Remcos or WannaCry attribution. HTTP and URLMon strings in the damaged resource remain references only.

trait_dispositions.relocated: PO-number basename matcher moves unchanged to metadata/file/naming::purchase-order-number-executable-name at notable; the name observes wording only. Explicit payment consumers are updated. No addition to the document-themed-executable-name umbrella, avoiding unintended membership expansion.
trait_dispositions.retired: The name+entropy, name+large-overlay, name+overlay-entropy, archive name+layout and .scr+bitmap+entropy conclusions lacked attack-specific execution evidence. Atomic properties remain visible. The direct CAB/PO consumer shared the unsupported name/layout premise and is retired.
trait_dispositions.dispatch: The CurrentDomain composite redundantly promoted an unrelated CLR reference. Retire it and retain the stronger concealed-PE/load/GetTypes/LateCall composite under an evidence-accurate name and description; co-occurrence does not prove a bound receiver.
trait_dispositions.native: Retain the four existing hostile code-oriented detections and injection/junk-padding observations. Descriptions correctly cover code in damaged installers without asserting successful installation.
trait_dispositions.reference_audit: Searched exact retired IDs and ancestor naming/masquerade homes. The relocated filename stops contributing to broad masquerade directory selectors intentionally; neutral naming selectors may now see the property. No active YAML references to retired IDs remain.
trait_dispositions.controls: Five static controls passed: original, renamed, invalid carrier magic, replaced late-call token, and an ordinary managed graphics fixture with inert random overlay and PO screensaver name. The last two non-concealment controls have zero hostile/suspicious findings.
trait_dispositions.naming_budget: The naming leaf was at 100 before relocation. Audited its rules and consolidated the short-stem TypeScript source/declaration atoms into short-stem-typescript-basename. Their only exact consumer was the same short-stem-script-basename OR. Type/platform/criticality, stem regex and exclusion lists remain identical; the suffix union is exact. Independent suffix/stem comparisons pass for 100 combinations. No new taxonomy branch or budget increase.
